title: Context and memory in an agent

items.stem: A student chats with your makerspace assistant on Monday and the session ends. On Thursday they open a new session and ask, "What did I book on Monday?" Nothing was saved anywhere. What can the assistant do?

options.text: Recall it, because the model keeps every past chat inside its weights
Recall it, because a large window holds all earlier sessions together
Not recall it, because the new context never contained that chat
Recall it, because the program resends old chats at every step

items.stem: An agent's first model call sends 2,000 tokens. It requests a tool that returns 500 tokens. The second call re-sends the history plus the tool request (50 tokens) and result, then the model writes a final answer. How many input tokens did the model read across both calls in total?
Your assistant must answer from a 150,000-token machine manual, and each question needs only one short section. Which design keeps the cost per request lowest?

options.text: Put the full manual in every call so nothing can be missed
Search the manual and load only the best few matching chunks
Pick a model with a bigger window and paste the manual once
Summarize the manual into one line and load that each call

items.stem: In one sentence: what must your program do so the assistant knows a student's training status in a brand-new session?
A retrieval search returns the wrong manual section, and the assistant answers confidently from it. In one sentence, why does the model not notice the mistake?
